title: Introduce regional anticipatory shepherd and soft preemptor
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During recent regional capacity spikes we observed rapid tenant thrashing that caused oscillating circuits and large KV cache churn. This PR introduces a regional anticipatory shepherd and a soft preemptor layer to reduce oscillation by gently preempting low-priority inflight work and priming circuit state before hard shedding. The goal is graceful degradation that avoids sudden tenant eviction while preserving SLOs for higher-priority cohorts. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add anticipatory_shepherd module that monitors short-window latency and queue growth and computes a preemptive target throttle level per-tenant; 2) control plane: add preemptor policy service that applies soft preemption (connection-level pacing and request-level deferral) with a bounded decay timer; 3) KV-preservation: introduce ephemeral KV-hinting to keep likely-hot keys in place during a soft preemption window; 4) telemetry: new metrics and traces to observe shepherd decisions and preemptor actions; 5) rollout: staged canary, config flags for soft_preempt_enabled and anticipatory_window_ms, and a fast rollback toggle. Implementation notes: The anticipatory_shepherd samples 1s and 10s quantiles and uses an exponential moving average to avoid reacting to single outliers. Decisions are batched and applied at the connection manager boundary so no per-request RPC is required. The preemptor uses a token-bucket style pacing that can temporarily reduce inflight tokens for tenant classes tagged as "best-effort". KV-hinting emits lightweight hints to the KV manager (no synchronous locking) and decays after the configured TTL. Backwards compatibility: All flags are off by default; the preemptor exposes a conservative safe-mode that emits telemetry but does not alter traffic. Testing: unit tests for the decision logic, integration test that replays a production traffic trace (tests/integration/regional_shepherd_test.go), and an e2e smoke harness used in CI. Rollout plan: 1) enable in staging for a week with verbose metrics; 2) canary 10% on a pick of regions with manual approval; 3) expand to 50% with auto-scaling guardrails; 4) full rollout once SLO regressions are <0.2% relative to baseline. Links: Linear ENG-3291 for design doc, runbook draft at docs/runbooks/regional-shepherd.md. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration trace replay [x] telemetry dashboards [x] runbook draft [x] feature flags gated [x] staged rollout plan documented. Why this is different: rather than immediate load-shedding or abrupt circuit tripping, this approach creates a short anticipatory window that primes circuits and slowly reduces low-priority concurrency to avoid cache churn and cascading slowdowns.

review_comments: Arjun Patel - Looks good overall. Concern: preemptor pacing could interact poorly with autoscaler; please add a safety clamp to avoid starving nodes. Requested change: add node-level min_tokens clamp and document expected interaction with autoscaler.
Maya Chen - Added a min_tokens clamp at the node level and documented the autoscaler interaction in docs/runbooks/regional-shepherd.md. Re-ran integration tests; results included in CI output.
Sofia Martinez - Telemetry is comprehensive. Suggestion: add a histogram for 'preemptor_decision_latency_ms' to ensure decisions are near-instant at scale. Can you add that to the metrics registry?
Maya Chen - Added histogram and a lightweight span; verified cost is negligible in staging trace replays.

Liam O'Connor - During a canary we saw one region where the preemptor caused a small but transient increase in tail p95. Please ensure the decay timer can be shortened for emergency rollback. Requested change: add emergency_rollback_ttl config and admin endpoint.
Maya Chen - emergency_rollback_ttl and admin endpoint added. Also added a toggle to instantly set soft_preempt_enabled=false via the admin API for fast rollback.

merge_summary: After addressing autoscaler clamp and emergency rollback TTL, reviewers approved. CI green after integration re-run. Merged via squash on 2025-02-03. Canary rollout initiated following merge with flags off by default.
release_notes: Introduce regional anticipatory shepherd and soft preemptor to reduce eviction churn during regional spikes. Adds feature flags for staged rollout and emergency rollback endpoints. No breaking changes. Observability added for decision tracing and preemptor metrics.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flags selectively in control plane: set soft_preempt_enabled=true only for canary regions. Watch metrics: shepherd_decisions_total, preemptor_actions_total, preemptor_decision_latency_ms, kv_hint_emits_total. Ops runbook at docs/runbooks/regional-shepherd.md contains rollback steps and autoscaler guidance.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Feature is opt-in and gated by flags. Main risk is interaction with autoscaling causing underprovisioning; node-level min_tokens clamp mitigates this. Emergency rollback endpoint provides fast disable path.
